clue.text: Missing company's tediously long work day at first

indicators.note: tells the solver that the working day's short form comes at the front, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: Friday is the last working day of the week, shortened to its calendar form
something that drags on without stopping seems never to end

explanation.surface: A dull, endless shift seems to leave a worker with no colleagues around them.
explanation.walkthrough: FRI is the calendar abbreviation for Friday, a working day.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking companions or allies is alone, without anyone at their side.

clue.text: Following great map

parts.note: ace is informal for excellent or first-rate

explanation.surface: Someone praises the map they are following.
explanation.walkthrough: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references. Map is old slang for the human face.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal British slang a person's map is their visage, the front of the head.

clue.text: Liberal gutlessly breaks vow, creating hostility

indicators.note: the shortened word breaks into the vow, sitting inside it

parts.note: I will is the promise spoken at a wedding

indicators.note: without its guts, the word keeps only its first and last letters

parts.note: the word Liberal, gutted, keeps only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A cowardly Liberal politician goes back on a promise and stirs up resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: The vow is the wedding-service response I WILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad feeling or animosity toward someone is the usual sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Victoria's neighbour has info released on law he's broken

indicators.note: places the last piece after the others in the down answer

parts.note: news is information about recent events
out means set free, as from prison

indicators.note: the letters of these words are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: the letters of these two words, taken as written, are the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A neighbour has news put out about a law someone has broken.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria is not a person but the Australian state, which borders the state named here.
explanation.definitionFit: This Australian state lies directly north and east of Victoria, sharing a long border with it.

clue.text: Fatty substance on rolls around food store

indicators.note: in a down answer the second piece comes on top of, after, the first

parts.note: lard is rendered pig fat used in cooking

indicators.note: rolling over turns the short word back to front

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Lard sits on bread rolls stored in the pantry.
explanation.definitionFit: A cool room or cupboard in which food is kept is the traditional name for a pantry.

clue.text: Grasp latte, removing partial stain left by liquid

indicators.note: only part of the run of words is used, so the answer lies inside them

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Someone grabs a coffee but needs to clean off a spill mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A splash or spattered mark from spilt liquid is what the noun describes.

clue.text: Recognise wonderful 12

indicators.note: the answer to 12 across means does spin, so the word is turned round

parts.note: tops is slang for the very best

explanation.surface: Someone recognises a great dance move from another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is the indicator: 12 across defines spinning, telling the solver to turn the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice or pick someone out is to identify them by sight.

clue.text: Treatment which won't really help identify personal problem

parts.note: to place someone is to recognise who they are
BO, body odour, is the classic embarrassing personal problem

explanation.surface: A doctor's remedy that cannot help pinpoint an embarrassing issue.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy pill given without active ingredients only works through a patient's belief.

clue.text: A doctor stops to wee? One might give this a shake

definitions.text: One might give this a shake

indicators.note: the pieces plug the short word like a stopper in a bottle

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
wee is informal for urine

explanation.surface: A doctor interrupts someone heading to the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is the shake after a wee; the instrument is in fact played by shaking.
explanation.definitionFit: This percussion instrument with jingles in its frame is played by shaking or striking it.

clue.text: Happy, say, briefly following officer in conflict

indicators.note: the dwarf comes after the officer

parts.note: Col is short for colonel

indicators.note: the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Happy is one of the Seven Dwarfs, so an example of a dwarf

explanation.surface: A cheerful officer briefly takes part in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Happy is one of the Seven Dwarfs in Snow White.
explanation.definitionFit: The decades of tense rivalry between the USA and Soviet Union are known by this name.

clue.text: It could prevent chaps I lead entering mall abroad

indicators.note: the short pieces go inside the jumbled word
abroad suggests going far and wide, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then jumbled
taken as written
Pb is the chemical symbol for lead

explanation.surface: Someone guides men into a shopping centre overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: Chaps is not men but cracked, sore skin on the lips.
explanation.definitionFit: A balm applied to the lips stops them from cracking and becoming sore in cold weather.

clue.text: Where to see King Charles put his foot down, stuck in job a long time

parts.note: a post is a position of employment
an age is a very long time
stamps means brings the foot down hard

explanation.surface: The King took a firm line, having been stuck in his role for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuck in job' plays on the long wait for the throne; the answer pictures the monarch's head on mail.
explanation.definitionFit: The monarch's head appears on British postage, so these are where his portrait is seen.

clue.text: Bounder, engaged by old PM with tips for elections, does spin

indicators.note: the bounder is held within the prime minister's name

parts.note: William Pitt was a British prime minister
a roué is a debauched man, a cad

indicators.note: the tips of the word are its first and last letters

parts.note: the word's first and last letters

explanation.surface: A cad, hired by a former prime minister to swing elections, spreads propaganda.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin' suggests political spin doctoring, but it means turning on the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballet dancer's full turn on one foot is the noun; here it is a verb, rotates.

clue.text: Energy firm doing its bit to save the planet

definitions.text: doing its bit to save the planet

explanation.surface: A green energy company promotes its environmental credentials.
explanation.definitionFit: The prefix or informal adjective describes things that are environmentally friendly.

clue.text: Someone watching you start to guzzle soup, tucking into German brew

indicators.note: the pieces tuck into the beer word, going inside it

parts.note: Bier is German for beer

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of this word
broth is a thin soup

explanation.surface: Someone watches you slurp soup while drinking German beer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four the all-seeing leader constantly observes citizens.

clue.text: Keys from hostel situated towards the west

indicators.note: in an across answer west is leftward, so the letters read backwards
the letters come from within the words

parts.note: the letters run from inside the first word into the second

explanation.surface: A traveller gets their keys from a hostel located in the west.
explanation.walkthrough: Keys are not door keys but low islands, as in the Florida Keys.
explanation.definitionFit: A key or cay is a small low island, so the plural means small islands.

clue.text: Assail extreme characters in bottle party

indicators.note: the extreme characters of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: only the first and last letters of this word are used
Labour is a UK political party

explanation.surface: Someone is attacked at a bottle party.
explanation.walkthrough: A bottle party is one where each guest brings a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: To attack verbally or physically, as in to belabour an opponent with criticism.

clue.text: Split region of Mali, a tad unsettled

indicators.note: letters not settled in place are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these words, taken as written, are rearranged

explanation.surface: A divided area of Mali is somewhat restless.
explanation.walkthrough: Split is not 'divided' but the Croatian city, the chief port of this coastal region.
explanation.definitionFit: Split is the main city of this historic Croatian coastal area on the Adriatic.

clue.text: What's good for a golfer, but bad for anyone else

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a score under the standard for a hole, which a golfer wants
second meaning: unwell or performing poorly, in everyday use

explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase is praise on the golf course and a complaint everywhere else.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the expected standard: a fine golf score but a sign of poor health or form elsewhere.

clue.text: Be dishonest about honey drink or fruit drink

indicators.note: the lie goes about the drink, surrounding it

parts.note: to lie is to be dishonest
mead is fermented honey and water

explanation.surface: Someone fibs over whether they had mead or a citrus drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetened drink made from the juice of a green citrus fruit.

clue.text: Jacob's son runs country club with Bill's partner

parts.note: the European Union is a club of countries
Bill and Ben are the Flowerpot Men of British children's television

explanation.surface: Someone runs a country club with a business partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill and Ben were the Flowerpot Men, a classic British children's TV pair.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the eldest of the twelve sons of the patriarch Jacob bears this name.

clue.text: One's husband is under caution, like Reading fans

indicators.note: in a down answer the later pieces sit under the first

parts.note: a footballer booked is given a caution by the referee
one's read as 'I is'

explanation.surface: A husband gets a yellow card, and Reading's supporters are among the onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is the English football club and town; the capital disguises 'reading' as in books.
explanation.definitionFit: People fond of reading books and studying are described as studious in this way.

clue.text: Upset, I appreciate that Brad is offensive

indicators.note: in a down answer upset means turned upside down, so read bottom to top

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
a brad is a small nail, as is a tack

explanation.surface: A thankful remark about Brad turns out to be insulting.
explanation.walkthrough: Brad looks like a name; it is a thin nail.
explanation.definitionFit: An offensive in war is an assault on the enemy, the noun sense of this word.

clue.text: Resistance unit that's surprising top spy

parts.note: oh is an exclamation of surprise
M is the head of MI6 in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: A resistance cell is startled by a senior agent.
explanation.definitionFit: The SI unit of electrical resistance is named after the physicist Georg Simon Ohm.

clue.text: Leader of lawmen taking off cap

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: its first letter alone
a take-off is a mimicking copy

explanation.surface: The chief of police removes his hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking off' suggests removing the cap, but it means mimicry.
explanation.definitionFit: A cap is a ceiling or restriction, as in a spending cap.

clue.text: Observed public disturbance, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the answer is pronounced like the word for the disturbance

parts.note: making a scene is causing a public fuss

explanation.surface: Someone noticed a fuss in public.
explanation.definitionFit: Past participle of the verb for noticing with the eyes.

clue.text: Tricked group, installing electronic phone device

parts.note: had means fooled, as in 'you've been had'
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A gang has been conned while fitting electronic phone equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Earphones with a microphone worn on the head, for making phone calls.

clue.text: Coat of amber silk fabric in wardrobe

indicators.note: the coat of a word is its outer letters

parts.note: only the outside letters of this word
moire is watered silk

explanation.surface: An amber silk coat hangs in the closet.
explanation.definitionFit: An armoire is a large, tall cupboard for clothes, from the French.

clue.text: European missing conclusion of ping pong

indicators.note: the European goes without the letter named

parts.note: a Greek is a European

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its last letter

parts.note: its final letter alone

letters that amaze are thrown into disorder
